assignments.reason: Clinging to the righteous (tzaddikim). In this Torah (line 8), the tzaddikim's essential function IS creating גבול וזמן (boundary and time) so that a person is not in a state of unstructured thirst (צמאון). The tzaddik operates within the vision/gazing domain — they enable proper ראיה by imposing limits. The Torah states 'מַעֲלַת הִתְדַּבְּקוּת בְּצַדִּיקִים כִּי הֵם עוֹשִׂים גְּבוּל וּזְמַן' — the essential virtue of the tzaddik is creating the vessel/boundary, which is Package 1's core mechanism. Polarity good: clinging to tzaddikim is a holy practice.

assignments.node_id: גבול וזמן, לבל יהיה בבחינת צמאון: וזה פרוש הפסוק: "צמאה נפשי לאלקים לאל חי", זה בחינת צמאון כנ"ל. "מתי אבוא" ולא יהא בבחינת צמאון. "ואראה פני אלקים", ואראה דיקא, דהינו שאזכה שתהיה העבודה בבחינת ראיה, שאזי הוא בבחינת גבול וזמן כראוי כנ"ל, ואזי אינו בבחינת צמאון כנ"ל
assignments.reason: This composite node describes the result of the tzaddik's intervention: creating boundary and time so one is no longer in a state of thirst, and instead achieves worship 'in the mode of seeing' (בחינת ראיה). Its essential nature is גבול וזמן — boundary and time — which is the core mechanism of Package 1 (vision/gazing creates vessels/limits). The node explicitly names ראיה as the desired state and גבול וזמן as its expression. Polarity good: this is the positive goal-state of proper structured worship.

Repentance from love. Its essential nature is defined by אהבה (love) — the qualifying word מאהבה makes love the defining quality of this type of repentance. The Torah (lines 14-15) says 'בִּתְשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה, שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁאֵר שׁוּם רֹשֶׁם כְּלָל' — love-based repentance leaves no stain, enabling שכל צח. It PRODUCES gadlut (cause-effect), but what it IS essentially is the love-quality (אהבה) applied to the process of return. Package 3 is the love/Abraham/expanded-mind domain, and תשובה מאהבה's defining character is that love. Polarity good: repentance from love is a holy spiritual practice.

Variant surface form of תשובה מאהבה (with the prefix ב meaning 'through/in'). Same essential nature: love-based repentance. The edge (id 3194) uses this form in the context 'אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בְּשֵׂכֶל צַח עַד שֶׁיָּשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה'. Its defining quality remains אהבה. Polarity good.

Kindnesses/mercies. The Torah (line 18) explicitly states 'מֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת חֲסָדִים וְרַחֲמִים' — gadlut IS chasadim and rachamim. Package 3 already contains the combined node 'רחמים וחסדים'. This standalone חסדים node has the same essential nature: it IS the attribute of kindness that characterizes the expanded-mind state. Polarity good: chasadim is a divine attribute of the right/holiness side.

Compassion/mercy. Same source as חסדים above: 'מֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת חֲסָדִים וְרַחֲמִים'. Rachamim IS the quality of the expanded mind. Package 3 already has 'רחמים וחסדים' as a combined node; this standalone רחמים has the same essential nature. The Talmudic proof (line 13) confirms: 'ה' הוּא רַחֲמִים'. Polarity good: divine compassion belongs to the holiness domain.

Expanded consciousness (mochin d'gadlut). This is a surface-form variant of 'גדלות המחין' which is already the dominant node of Package 3. The packages file notes a parallel alias case: 'קטנות המחין' and 'מחין דקטנות' are the same concept in Package 2. Similarly, מחין דגדלות = גדלות המחין. Its essential nature is the expanded, merciful, love-sourced state of consciousness — the core of Package 3. Polarity good.

assignments.node_id: לנסות ולהרים את בחינת המחין דקטנות, שהם בחינת אלקים
assignments.reason: To test and elevate the aspect of smallness-of-mind which is the aspect of Elohim. This node describes the object of the elevation process — the מוחין דקטנות/אלהים state. The node's identity is defined by the katnut/Elohim/din concepts it names: it IS the katnut state being acted upon. While the act of elevating is positive, the node as a concept refers to and is constituted by the constrained-intellect domain (Package 2). The text (line 18): 'לְנַסּוֹת וּלְהָרִים אֶת בְּחִינַת הַמֹּחִין דְּקַטְנוּת, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת אֱלֹקִים'. Polarity evil: the node names and describes the katnut/Elohim/din state.

Creates a vessel, boundary, and time. This is the effect-node of בטחון/הסתכלות (edges 2365, 2366). Its essential nature is כלי/גבול וזמן — the vessel/boundary concept that the additions file already identified as belonging to Package 1 (node 'כלי / גבול וזמן'). The Torah (line 5): 'הִסְתַּכְּלוּת עוֹשָׂה כְּלִי, דְּהַיְנוּ גְּבוּל וּזְמַן'. Boundary-and-time is the structural mechanism of vision, not inherently good or evil. Polarity neutral.

Gazing in trust. This is a composite of הסתכלות and בטחון, both already core members of Package 1. The Torah (line 6): 'עַל־יְדֵי הִסְתַּכְּלוּת בְּבִטָּחוֹן גַּם כֵּן עוֹשֶׂה כְּלִי'. Its essential nature IS the gazing/trust domain. Polarity good: this is the active spiritual practice of fixing one's gaze on God in trust.

assignments.node_id: עושה לההשפעה גבול וזמן, שתבוא השפע בעת וזמן שהוא צריך
assignments.reason: Creates for the divine flow (hashpa'a) a boundary and time, so the shefa arrives when needed. A more detailed variant of עושה כלי וגבול וזמן, describing the same mechanism applied to divine abundance. Its essential nature is גבול וזמן — the vessel/boundary concept of Package 1. The Torah (line 6): 'עוֹשֶׂה לְהַהַשְׁפָּעָה גְּבוּל וּזְמַן, שֶׁתָּבוֹא הַשֶּׁפַע בְּעֵת וּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא צָרִיךְ'. Polarity neutral: boundary-and-time applied to divine flow is a structural mechanism.

Prayer with clear intellect. While prayer is a spiritual practice, this specific form of prayer is defined by its שכל צח (clear intellect) quality — the additions file placed שכל צח in Package 3 as a bechina of גדלות המחין. The Torah (lines 12, 15) describes this as the ability that comes with having a luminous mind: 'מִי שֶׁמֹּחוֹ צַח, וְיָכוֹל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל... בְּלִי עִיּוּן'. The qualifying phrase 'בשכל צח' makes the clear-intellect quality the defining characteristic. This Torah does not have a separate prayer package; the concept's essential nature is the gadlut/expanded-mind state expressed through worship. Polarity good: prayer with clear mind is the Torah's positive goal.
